samples.content:
<repaired_code>
import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class B {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        String[] tokens = reader.readLine().trim().split("\\s+");
        int n = Integer.parseInt(tokens[0]);
        double p = Double.parseDouble(tokens[1]);

        // We need to find the minimum number of maps k to study such that
        // the probability that at least one of the maps played is studied is at least p.
        
        // The game selects 3 random maps from n.
        // Each player (Johnny and opponent) discards one map from the 3.
        // The system then randomly selects one of the maps not discarded by either player.
        
        // For Johnny to play a studied map, at least one studied map must survive
        // both players' discards and be selected.
        
        // Let's think about the probability that a particular studied map is played.
        // But it's easier to compute the probability that NO studied map is played,
        // then subtract from 1.
        
        // If Johnny studies k maps, there are n-k unstudied maps.
        // For no studied map to be played, all 3 selected maps must include only unstudied maps,
        // AND both players must discard in such a way that an unstudied map survives.
        
        // Actually, let's reconsider the process:
        // 1. System picks 3 maps uniformly at random from n maps.
        // 2. Johnny sees these 3 maps and must discard one.
        // 3. Opponent sees the same 3 maps and discards one uniformly at random.
        // 4. The system picks one of the maps not discarded by either player uniformly at random.
        
        // Johnny's optimal strategy: If there are s studied maps among the 3, he should discard an unstudied one if possible.
        // So:
        // - If all 3 are unstudied (s=0): Johnny discards any (all unstudied), opponent discards randomly.
        // - If 2 unstudied, 1 studied (s=1): Johnny discards an unstudied, opponent discards randomly.
        // - If 1 unstudied, 2 studied (s=2): Johnny discards the unstudied, opponent discards randomly.
        // - If 3 studied (s=3): Johnny discards any (all studied), opponent discards randomly.
        
        // We want the probability that the final map is studied to be >= p.
        
        // Let's compute the probability for each possible number of studied maps in the initial 3:
        // C(k, s) * C(n-k, 3-s) / C(n, 3) for s = 0, 1, 2, 3
        
        // Then for each case, compute the probability that a studied map is played.
        
        int answer = 0;
        for (int k = 0; k <= n; k++) {
            double probStudied = 0.0;
            
            for (int s = 0; s <= 3 && s <= k && (3-s) <= (n-k); s++) {
                // Probability that exactly s studied maps are in the initial 3
                long waysToChooseStudied = comb(k, s);
                long waysToChooseUnstudied = comb(n-k, 3-s);
                long totalWays = comb(n, 3);
                
                double probS = (double)(waysToChooseStudied * waysToChooseUnstudied) / totalWays;
                
                // Now compute probability that a studied map is played given s studied maps in the 3
                double probPlayedGivenS = 0.0;
                
                if (s == 0) {
                    // All 3 are unstudied, so no studied map can be played
                    probPlayedGivenS = 0.0;
                } else if (s == 1) {
                    // 1 studied, 2 unstudied
                    // Johnny will discard an unstudied (2 choices)
                    // Opponent discards randomly among 3 maps
                    
                    // Cases for opponent's discard:
                    // - Opponent discards the studied map (prob 1/3): then both unstudied remain, system picks unstudied
                    // - Opponent discards an unstudied map (prob 2/3): 
                    //   - If opponent discards the same unstudied as Johnny (prob 1/2 of this case): 2 maps remain (1 studied, 1 unstudied), system picks studied with prob 1/2
                    //   - If opponent discards the other unstudied (prob 1/2 of this case): 1 unstudied remains, system picks unstudied
                    
                    // Actually, let's be more precise:
                    // Johnny picks one of the 2 unstudied to discard.
                    // Opponent picks uniformly at random among the 3 maps.
                    
                    // If opponent picks studied (1/3): remaining maps are the 2 unstudied, system picks unstudied -> 0
                    // If opponent picks unstudied A (1/3): 
                    //   - If Johnny discarded A: remaining are studied and unstudied B -> system picks studied with prob 1/2
                    //   - If Johnny discarded B: remaining are studied and unstudied A -> system picks studied with prob 1/2
                    // If opponent picks unstudied B (1/3): similar to above
                    
                    // Since Johnny will discard an unstudied, and there are 2 unstudied, let's say A and B.
                    // Opponent picks A with prob 1/3, B with prob 1/3, studied with prob 1/3.
                    
                    // If opponent picks A: 
                    //   - If Johnny discarded A: remaining = {studied, B}, system picks studied with prob 1/2
                    //   - If Johnny discarded B: remaining = {studied, A}, system picks studied with prob 1/2
                    // But Johnny can choose which unstudied to discard. He'll choose optimally.
                    // Actually, since both unstudied are equivalent, Johnny's choice doesn't matter for probability.
                    // So given opponent picks an unstudied, the probability studied is played is 1/2.
                    
                    // So overall: prob = (1/3)*0 + (2/3)*(1/2) = 1/3
                    
                    probPlayedGivenS = 1.0 / 3.0;
                } else if (s == 2) {
                    // 2 studied, 1 unstudied
                    // Johnny will discard the unstudied (only one choice to maximize his chance)
                    // Opponent discards randomly among 3 maps
                    
                    // Opponent picks unstudied (1/3): remaining = 2 studied, system picks studied with prob 1
                    // Opponent picks studied A (1/3): remaining = {studied B, unstudied}, system picks studied with prob 1/2
                    // Opponent picks studied B (1/3): similar to above, prob 1/2
                    
                    // So overall: (1/3)*1 + (2/3)*(1/2) = 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3
                    
                    probPlayedGivenS = 2.0 / 3.0;
                } else if (s == 3) {
                    // All 3 studied
                    // Johnny discards any (all studied), opponent discards randomly
                    
                    // Opponent picks any map (1/3 each), remaining 2 are studied, system picks studied with prob 1
                    
                    probPlayedGivenS = 1.0;
                }
                
                probStudied += probS * probPlayedGivenS;
            }
            
            if (probStudied >= p) {
                answer = k;
                break;
            }
        }
        
        System.out.println(answer);
    }
    
    private static long comb(int n, int k) {
        if (k < 0 || k > n) return 0;
        if (k == 0 || k == n) return 1;
        
        long result = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
            result = result * (n - i + 1) / i;
        }
        return result;
    }
}
</repaired_code>
